summary: Chat streaming truncated after transient pipeline reset for dedicated customer
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that SSE/WebSocket streaming responses abruptly truncate mid-sentence following short transient errors in the serving pipeline (worker restart / routing flip). Impact: customer chat sessions for multiple users end with partial output (last token(s) missing), leading to degraded UX and automated retry loops on their side. Environment: LexiVoice dedicated cluster in us-west-2, running dedicated pool rp-lexivoice-usw2 on redwood-rlhf-13b pinned version v2026-02-28. Observed intermittently starting 2026-03-10 18:12 UTC and reproducible for customer under bursty input patterns (20-30 concurrent long-form chats).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use LexiVoice account credentials to send a streaming chat request to /v1/chat with stream=true and model=redwood-rlhf-13b (pinned).
2) Send a long prompt that triggers ~800-1200 token response (typical LexiVoice assistant reply),
3) Simulate burst concurrency: 20 simultaneous streaming requests from distinct client sockets,
4) While streams are in-flight, trigger a light worker restart or cause a routing update (in test: toggle an autoscaler event or redeploy a serving worker).
5) Observe that a subset (~5-12%) of client streams terminate with a final socket close before end-of-stream token; no explicit 5xx returned to client.
observed_behavior: Streaming socket closes without final chunk and without explicit error payload. Client receives partial text and then a TCP FIN/WS close. On platform side, logs show a short-lived pipeline reset (worker SIGTERM and graceful restart) correlated with router reassignments. No 5xx spike on public API layer, but internal worker logs show 'inflight-request-evicted' and 'kv-cache-miss -> eviction' in proximity.
expected_behavior: Streaming responses should continue to completion or, if interrupted, return a clear error frame (HTTP 5xx or SSE event) and ensure client can resume or receive a final summary chunk. Model fallback or worker restart should trigger graceful draining of in-flight streams rather than silent truncation.
recent_logs: 2026-03-10T18:12:23Z router[router-23]: reassigning request id=aa3f... to worker w-772 due to capacity reshuffle
2026-03-10T18:12:23Z worker[w-771]: SIGTERM received, beginning graceful shutdown, inflight=7
2026-03-10T18:12:24Z worker[w-771]: kv-cache eviction triggered for model redwood-rlhf-13b shard=2
2026-03-10T18:12:24Z api-gateway[gw-9]: downstream connection closed by peer for client c-984 (status unknown)
investigation_notes: Initial triage: patterns point to graceful shutdown window not fully draining SSE/WS streams when a worker is restarted under load; router reassigns requests mid-generation rather than waiting for completion.
Hypothesis A: draining timeout on worker is too short under long-response workloads leading to abrupt close before remote worker can finish sending final chunks.

Hypothesis B: KV cache miss when reassigning a long-running request causes partial output to be lost when the new worker cannot reconstruct the current generation state quickly, leading to immediate connection termination.

Temporary reproduction in staging: forced SIGTERM with 5s drain results in ~40% of streams truncating; increasing drain to 30s eliminated truncation in staging tests but increased tail latency and backpressure on autoscaler.
Observation: api-gateway does not always surface a 502/503 to client when downstream closes mid-stream; need to verify gateway stream-forwarding behavior on abrupt downstream close.
comments: LexiVoice (customer) - 2026-03-10 18:45 UTC: We're seeing our users get partial replies frequently this evening. No consistent error codes on our side; clients just receive truncated text. Please prioritize.
Support (Aisha) - 2026-03-10 19:00 UTC: Thanks — triaging now. Can you provide 3 sample request IDs and approximate timestamps? Also confirm whether you use exponential backoff retries client-side.
LexiVoice - 2026-03-10 19:07 UTC: Sample request IDs: aa3f4c2b, b9f2d001, c7a1e33e. We do a single immediate retry on client timeout; not exponential.

SRE (Ben) - 2026-03-10 20:10 UTC: Reproduced in staging by forcing worker restarts. Short-term mitigation: increasing worker graceful-drain to 30s reduced truncation rate to near 0 in staging. However, this impacted autoscaling responsiveness.

Eng (Carla) - 2026-03-11 09:12 UTC: Noted kv-cache rebuild on takeover is expensive for large-context requests; propose warm handoff where router waits for new worker to prefetch KV context before reassigning the stream. Filing platform design spike.

Support (Aisha) - 2026-03-12 08:22 UTC: Applied temporary config change to LexiVoice dedicated pool: increased drain timeout and enabled connection-close-propagation flag on gateway. Observing fewer truncations in last 12 hours.
next_steps: 1) Engineering to implement prefetch warm-handoff prototype (router waits for KV sync) — tracked in PR #889.
2) Adjust worker graceful-drain default to 20s for dedicated pools with long-response heuristics while we evaluate tail effects.
3) Modify api-gateway to translate downstream abrupt closes to explicit 5xx frames for streaming clients to make failure visible to customers.
4) Run a controlled canary on LexiVoice pool with warm-handoff enabled and monitor truncation rate and autoscaler behavior for 72 hours.
5) Postmortem and customer communication draft once canary completes.
resolution: In Progress: temporary mitigations applied (increased drain timeout, gateway close propagation). Engineering has a design spike and a PR prototype for warm-handoff. Tracking canary rollout and will follow up with permanent fix and postmortem.
customer_impact_summary: Multiple LexiVoice production chat sessions experienced truncated streaming replies, impacting end-user experience and causing retries. Affects ~5-12% of long-form streaming requests under bursty concurrency in their dedicated pool.
time_to_detect: ~3 minutes from first occurrence to automated alert via streaming-health monitor
estimated_workaround_risk: Low (increasing drain increases tail latency/pressure on autoscaler)
